The Flutter App Development internship in short

In the SkillMe Flutter App Development internship you build one of 3 projects, such as FitPulse: Modern Mobile Fitness & Workout Companion, a project where you build a simple workout tracker app where you can plan workouts, log them, and see your weekly progress. In week 1 you set up Flutter and build the first two static screens of FitPulse: a home dashboard and a list of workouts. By week 4 you finish FitPulse as a portfolio-ready app. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

What you build

One of 3 real projects, built over four weeks

You are assigned one of these projects when you start, and build it milestone by milestone.

FitPulse: Modern Mobile Fitness & Workout Companion

Build a simple workout tracker app where you can plan workouts, log them, and see your weekly progress.

  1. W1Home Screen & Workout List with Widgets
  2. W2Add Workouts with Forms & Navigation
  3. W3Save Data Locally & Workout History
  4. W4Provider, Weekly Chart & Release Build

WalletWave: Personal Finance & Smart Budget Tracker

Build an expense tracker app that records your income and spending and shows where your money goes each month.

  1. W1Balance Dashboard & Transaction List
  2. W2Add, Edit & Delete Transactions

  4. W4Budgets, Pie Chart & Release Build

Week by week

What each week of the Flutter App Development internship covers

Shown for FitPulse: Modern Mobile Fitness & Workout Companion. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Home Screen & Workout List with Widgets

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Set up Flutter and build the first two static screens of FitPulse: a home dashboard and a list of workouts. Everything uses hardcoded data this week, so you can focus completely on how widgets and layouts fit together.

    What you learn

    • How a Flutter app is structured: main(), MaterialApp, Scaffold and the widget tree
    • Layout widgets: Column, Row, Padding, Container, Expanded and SizedBox
    • Showing lists of data with ListView.builder and Card/ListTile
    • Creating a simple Dart model class and your own reusable widget

    What you submit

    • A Flutter project in a public GitHub repo
    • A Home screen with summary cards and a Workouts screen with a scrollable list
    • A reusable WorkoutCard widget and a Workout model class
    • A README with setup steps and at least one screenshot
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • The app runs without errors on an emulator, phone or Chrome
    • The bottom navigation switches between the Home and Workouts screens
    • The workout list is built from a Dart list with ListView.builder, not copy-pasted widgets
    • The workout card UI lives in its own widget file
    • The repo contains a README with a screenshot

    Stretch goal: Add a simple circular progress indicator on the home screen showing 'workouts done this week out of your weekly goal'.

  2. Week 2 of 4

    Add Workouts with Forms & Navigation

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Make FitPulse interactive: users can add new workouts through a form, open a workout's detail screen, and mark it as done. This week teaches you how Flutter apps change what is on screen when data changes.

    What you learn

    • The difference between StatelessWidget and StatefulWidget, and when to call setState
    • Moving between screens with Navigator.push and Navigator.pop, including passing data back
    • Building forms with Form, TextFormField, DropdownButtonFormField and validators
    • Updating a list in memory and seeing the UI refresh

    What you submit

    • An Add Workout form with validation
    • A Workout Detail screen opened from the list
    • Mark-as-done and delete actions that update the UI immediately
    • A 30-60 second screen recording of the flow
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • Submitting the form with an empty name or invalid duration shows an error and does not save
    • A valid new workout appears in the list right after saving
    • Tapping a workout opens its detail screen and the back button returns to the list
    • Marking a workout as done updates the summary card on the Home screen
    • Deleting a workout removes it and shows a SnackBar

    Stretch goal: Add a filter row of ChoiceChips at the top of the list to show only one category at a time.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    Save Data Locally & Workout History

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Right now all workouts disappear when the app restarts. This week you save them on the device and add a history of completed workouts, handling loading and errors properly so the app never shows a blank or broken screen.

    What you learn

    • Local storage on the device with shared_preferences or Hive
    • Converting objects to and from JSON with toJson() and fromJson()
    • Async code in Dart: Future, async and await
    • Showing loading, empty and error states in the UI

    What you submit

    • Workouts that persist across full app restarts
    • A WorkoutStorage class that handles saving and loading
    • A History screen showing completed workouts with dates
    • Loading, empty and error states in the UI
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • Adding a workout, fully closing the app and reopening it still shows that workout
    • Completed workouts appear on the History screen with the date they were completed
    • A loading indicator is visible while data loads
    • With no workouts saved, the list shows a helpful empty-state message instead of a blank screen
    • Storage errors are caught and do not crash the app

    Stretch goal: Add a simple rest timer screen that counts down from a chosen number of seconds using Timer.periodic.

  4. Week 4 of 4

    Provider, Weekly Chart & Release Build

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Finish FitPulse as a portfolio-ready app. You will move your data into a simple Provider so any screen can use it, add a weekly progress chart, polish the design, and produce an installable build with a demo video.

    What you learn

    • Simple app-wide state management with provider and ChangeNotifier
    • Drawing a bar chart from your own data with a chart package such as fl_chart
    • Adding a dark theme and small polish details
    • Building a release APK or a web build

    What you submit

    • App state managed with Provider
    • A Progress screen with a 7-day bar chart
    • A release APK (attached to a GitHub Release) or a web build
    • A polished README and a 60-second demo video
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • Workout data is read and changed through a Provider, not passed through constructors
    • The chart shows correct minutes for the last 7 days and updates when a workout is completed
    • Light and dark themes both look readable
    • A release APK or web build is available from the repo
    • The README explains features, setup and includes screenshots

    Stretch goal: Add a daily reminder with a local notifications package, or write two widget tests for the Add Workout form.

Is it for you?

This internship fits you if

  • You know the basics of Dart, Flutter and Cross-Platform and want a real project to show for it, not more tutorials.

  • You can give it about 2-3 hours a week around college or a job, from any country.

Flutter App Development internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the Flutter App Development internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: FitPulse: Modern Mobile Fitness & Workout Companion, WalletWave: Personal Finance & Smart Budget Tracker or RecipeRadar: Recipe Finder App with a Free Public API. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the Flutter App Development internship?

The Flutter App Development internship works with Dart, Flutter and Cross-Platform. Week 1: how a Flutter app is structured: main(), MaterialApp, Scaffold and the widget tree; layout widgets: Column, Row, Padding, Container, Expanded and SizedBox. Week 2: the difference between StatelessWidget and StatefulWidget, and when to call setState; moving between screens with Navigator.push and Navigator.pop, including passing data back. Week 3: local storage on the device with shared_preferences or Hive; converting objects to and from JSON with toJson() and fromJson(). Week 4: simple app-wide state management with provider and ChangeNotifier; drawing a bar chart from your own data with a chart package such as fl_chart.

Do I need experience to apply for the Flutter App Development internship?

You need the basics of Dart, Flutter and Cross-Platform, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you set up Flutter and build the first two static screens of FitPulse: a home dashboard and a list of workouts. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each Flutter App Development milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of FitPulse: Modern Mobile Fitness & Workout Companion, that means: the app runs without errors on an emulator, phone or Chrome; the bottom navigation switches between the Home and Workouts screens; the workout list is built from a Dart list with ListView.builder, not copy-pasted widgets; the workout card UI lives in its own widget file; the repo contains a README with a screenshot. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the Flutter App Development internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Built the first screens of a Flutter fitness app with a dashboard and workout list; Created a reusable workout card widget and a Dart model class; Set up bottom navigation and a consistent app theme using Material widgets; Added a validated form to create new workouts in my Flutter app; Implemented screen navigation with data passed between screens; Used StatefulWidget and setState to mark workouts done and delete them with instant UI updates; Added local data persistence to my Flutter fitness app so workouts survive restarts; Built a workout history screen using JSON serialisation and async Dart code; Handled loading, empty and error states for a smoother user experience; Completed FitPulse, a Flutter workout tracker with local storage and Provider state management; Built a weekly progress bar chart and a dark theme; Shipped a release build with a documented README and demo video.

What are the other projects in the Flutter App Development internship?

WalletWave: Personal Finance & Smart Budget Tracker: Build an expense tracker app that records your income and spending and shows where your money goes each month. RecipeRadar: Recipe Finder App with a Free Public API: Build a recipe app that searches real recipes from a free online API and lets you save your favourites. Every project follows the same four-week shape, with one reviewed milestone a week.

Is the Flutter App Development internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based and goes to the interns whose reviewed Flutter App Development work stands out in their cohort, not to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
